etymologies.etymologyHTML: From regard +‎ -less.

definitions.definition: Without attention to warnings or indications of bad consequences.

quote.citation: 1764 December 24 (indicated as 1765), Onuphrio Muralto, translated by William Marshal [pseudonyms; Horace Walpole], chapter V, in The Castle of Otranto, […], London:  […]  Tho[mas] Lownds […], →OCLC, pages 190–191:
quote.text: Hippolita, ſcarce more alive than her daughter, was regardleſs of every thing but her: but when the tender Iſabella’s care would have likewiſe removed her, while the ſurgeons examined Matilda’s wound, ſhe cried, remove me! never! never! I lived but in her, and will expire with her.

definitions.definition: Taking insufficient regard of; heedless; careless.

quote.citation: 1815 December (indicated as 1816), [Jane Austen], chapter XV, in Emma: […], volume III, London:  […]  [Charles Roworth and James Moyes] for John Murray, →OCLC, page 279:
quote.text: Always deceived in fact by his own wishes, and regardless of little besides his own convenience.

quote.citation: 1843, Edgar Allan Poe, The Black Cat:
quote.text: I grew, day by day, more moody, more irritable, more regardless of the feelings of others.

definitions.definition: (proscribed) Synonym of regardless of; paying no attention to.
